**1.2 Drive System Choices**

**1.2.1 Motor Selection**

The following table shows the comparison between the LEGO EV3 Medium Motor and EV3 Large Motor based on four main criteria. 

| Criteria | EV3 Medium Motor | EV3 Large Motor |
| ----- | :---: | :---: |
| **Motor Photo** | ![][image1] | ![][image2] |
| **Torque (Running Torque)**  | 6.64 N·cm  | 17.3 N·cm  |
| **Speed (No-load)**  | 165 RPM  | 105 RPM |
| **Part Number**  | 45503  | 45502  |
| **Key Feature**  | Compact and lightweight; higher rotational speed  | Higher torque;  suitable for heavy loads  |

* We selected the **EV3 Medium Servo Motor** because our robot weighs approximately 800 g and does not require the high torque provided by the EV3 Large Servo Motor.   
* With a maximum speed of 165 RPM, the Medium Motor offers higher rotational speed compared to the Large Motor (105 RPM). In our actual operation, we typically use only 65% of the motor speed, which is sufficient to move our robot effectively.  
* Therefore, the Medium Motor provides an ideal balance of speed, torque, and compactness without requiring the additional torque of a larger motor.

**Testing Performance for Motor Selection**

| Parameters  | EV3 Medium Motor | EV3 Large Motor  |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Motor Speed**  | 100% | 100%  |
| **Total Testing Rounds**  | 10 | 10 |
| **Successful Rounds**  | **9** | **2** |
| **Failed Rounds**  | 1 | 8 |
| **Success Rate**  | 90% | 20% |
| **Average Completion Time**  | 25.67s | 18s |

**Engineering Decision：**

* The EV3 Medium Motor was selected instead of the EV3 Large Motor based on its higher reliability during the Open Challenge testing at 100% speed.   
* The Medium Motor achieved a 100% success rate (6/6 trials) with an average completion time of 25.67 seconds, while the Large Motor achieved only a 20% success rate (2/10 trials) despite being faster, with an average completion time of 18 seconds.   
* Although the Large Motor offered better speed, the Medium Motor provided more consistent performance.   
* Therefore, reliability and successful navigation were prioritised over maximum speed. 

**1.2.2 Gear Combination Selection**

To further minimize the drivetrain size, we designed a compact gearbox using:

| ![][image3] | ![][image4] | ![][image5] |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 1 piece Z20 Double Bevel Gear (20 Teeth) – Part 18575 | 1 piece Differential Gear (28 Teeth) – Part 62821 | 3 piece Conical Wheels (12 Teeth) – Part 6589  |

**Gear Ratio Calculation**

| DrivenGearTeeth \= 28T DrivingGearTeeth \= 20T Motor Speed \= 165RPM Torque \= 6.64 N.CM |
| :---: |

| ![][image6] | $GearRatio\ \ \ \ \ \ =\frac{DrivenGearTeeth}{DrivingGearTeeth}$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =\frac{28T}{20T}$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =\ 1.4:1$   $OutputSpeed\ \ =\frac{InputSpeed}{GearRatio}$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =\frac{165}{1.4}$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =$ $117.86RPM$  $OutputTorque\ \ \ \ =Motor\ Torque\ ×\ Gear\ Ratio$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =$ 6.64 $×$ 1.4 ${}$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =$ 9.296 N·cm  |
| :---: | :---- |

* We selected a 1.4:1 gear reduction to balance motor speed and output torque. The 20T Z20 Double Bevel Gear transfers power from the EV3 Medium Motor to the 28T Differential Gear.   
* This reduction decreases rotational speed while increasing the theoretical output torque.  
* The differential gearbox, which contains three internal 12T bevel gears, distributes power to the left and right drive wheels while allowing them to rotate at different speeds during turns.   
* This helps the robot navigate corners smoothly while maintaining stable movement.

**1.2.3 Drive System Choices Reasoning （Ideal Force & Thrust-to-Weight Ratio)**

**Selected Drive System Parameters** 

| Parameter  | Selected Value/Items |
| :---: | :---: |
| **Motor**  | EV3 Medium Motor  |
| **Gear Ratio**  | 1.4:1  |
| **Motor Torque**  | 6.64 N·cm  |
| **Motor Speed** | 165 RPM  |
| **Output Torque,${T}_{out}$**  | 9.296 N·cm  |
| **Output Speed**  | 117.86 RPM  |
| **Wheel**  | LEGO 32019 \+ 86652  |
| **Wheel Radius,r** | 31.2 mm  |
| **Robot Mass,m**  | 800g |
| **Gravity (g)** | 9.81 m/s²  |

| Driving Force Calculation (F) | Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR)  |
| :---: | :---: |
| $F=\frac{{T}_{out}}{r}$ $\ \ \ =\frac{0.09296}{0.0312}$     $=$ 2.98N | $TWR=\frac{F}{m\times g}$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =\frac{2.98}{0.8\times 9.81}$ $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ =0.38:1$ |

* The EV3 Medium Motor with a 1.4:1 gear reduction was selected because it provides a suitable balance between driving force and output speed.   
* The calculated driving force of 2.98 N and TWR of 0.38:1 are considered suitable for the 0.8 kg robot, while maintaining a compact drivetrain design.
